prompt:
Platform automation ticket. Our VCF 9.1 inventory collector talks directly to the vCenter vSphere Automation API. It currently trusts collection order and holds one API access token forever. During a real run the token expired after the VM request but before the host request; the collector restarted from the beginning, duplicated work, and produced a differently ordered snapshot. Build package vcenter at this module's root, using only the Go standard library.

Research before changing code. Use genuine web research to read the pinned official OpenAPI source itself, not a rendered documentation page: the Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository at the commit and path recorded in docs/official_sources.json. Confirm the repository permalink, the raw specification, its license, and the three exact operationIds named there. Cite the exact official URLs you read in your final response. docs/contract.json is a protected extraction of that specification; if a later branch or rendered page differs, mention it and keep the pinned contract and fixtures unchanged.

Implement this public surface:

- `NewClient(Config) (*Client, error)`, where `Config` has `BaseURL`, `AccessToken`, `SubjectToken`, and `SubjectTokenType` strings plus `HTTPClient *http.Client` (nil means `http.DefaultClient`). BaseURL is an absolute vCenter origin; reject missing credentials and malformed/non-origin URLs.
- `(*Client).Inventory(ctx context.Context) (Inventory, error)`. `Inventory` contains `VMs []VM` and `Hosts []Host`. `VM` exposes the spec fields `ID`, `Name`, `PowerState`, optional `CPUCount`, and optional `MemorySizeMiB`. `Host` exposes `ID`, `Name`, `ConnectionState`, optional `PowerState`, and optional `HostUUID`.
- Retrieve VMs first with `Vcenter.VM_list`, then hosts with `Vcenter.Host_list`. Use the exact paths, JSON field names, success statuses, Accept header, and `vmware-api-session-id` security scheme pinned in docs/contract.json. Sort each returned collection lexicographically by its identifier before returning it; server order is deliberately unstable.
- If either collection request returns 401, call `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue` exactly once using the pinned form-encoded token-exchange fields and federated Bearer credential, replace the access token, and retry only that failed collection request once. Do not restart Inventory or discard the collection already fetched. A second 401 is returned as `*APIError`. Concurrent callers that fail with the same stale access token must share one exchange; callers arriving after rotation reuse the new token.
- Decode vAPI collection failures into `*APIError` with `StatusCode`, `ErrorType`, and the complete `Messages` array (`id`, `default_message`, `args`). Decode token endpoint failures into `*TokenError` with `StatusCode`, `Code`, `Description`, and `URI`. Both implement `error`. Context cancellation must remain discoverable with `errors.Is`.

Acceptance is table-driven `inventory_test.go` plus the protected loopback service in `internal/contractmock`. The mock exposes an in-memory request log, serves only the three operationIds in the pinned contract, expires the first access token partway through Inventory, and flips collection element order on every successful response. No live VMware endpoint or real credential is used by verification. Run `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`. Do not edit inventory_test.go, internal/contractmock/server.go, or anything under docs/.

official_sources.title: vSphere Automation API 9.1 OpenAPI specification at the pinned VCF 9.1 release commit
official_sources.used_for: Exact paths, operationIds, security schemes, form and JSON media types, status codes, and request/response schemas

official_sources.title: Raw vcenter.yaml at the pinned commit
official_sources.used_for: Machine-readable source from which docs/contract.json was extracted

research.language_rationale: The official VCF 9.1 repository supplies an OpenAPI contract and supported Java/Python SDKs but no generated Go module for this surface. A focused standard-library net/http package is appropriate for a Go inventory pipeline and keeps token rotation behavior explicit.
